newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 30.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:

* U.S stocks rolled to another record Tuesday, while a rally in the bond market drove interest rates to their lowest levels in nearly eight months. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 53.42 points to 8,174.53, the second consecutive record for the blue-chip average and the fifth in the last six sessions.
* On Tuesday, Indonesia's central bank said that the rupiah had returned to a normal trading range in recent days after reaching a record low last week in the wake of an attack by speculators.

* On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index closed up 0.78 percent at 716.36 points as investors bought back several blue chip stocks, particularly Telkom and Bank Negara Indonesia, on the back of a stable rupiah, brokers said.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was traded at 2,560.00/2,580.00 at 0217 GMT against an opening of 2,565.00/2,575.00
* Finance company Putra Surya following news that it posted a first-half net profit of 101.07 billion rupiah, compared with 18.87 billion rupiah in the same 1996 period.

* Blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia after its shareholders apporoved a new board of directors at an extraordinary general meeting on Tuesday. The bank's president director Widigdo Sukarman also said that it is in the process of buying a stake in N.V. De Indonesische Overzeese Bank (Indover) in Amsterdam.
* Bank Niaga following news that the Tirtamas Group, which has announced the acquisition of the bank, believes the deal will provide synergies with its other banking and insurance businesses.
* Pharmaceutical firm PT Dankos Laboratories on news that its first-half net profit was 12.09 billion rupiah, against 11.25 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.
* Indonesian insurance company Lippo Life following reports that it posted a net profit of 65.8 billion rupiah in the first half of 1997, against 14 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.

* Small property firm Mas Murni after Bisnis Indonesia quoted the company's president director Djaja Santosa as saying that it had signed an agreement to set up a joint-venture with Hong Kong-based Lintel Hospitality Consultants to develop its hotel business. He also said that the firm had targeted a profit growth of 20 percent for 1997.
* Property firm Royal Sentul Highlands on its encouraging debut on Monday.
